barren.songTitle: Yankee Bayonet (I Will Be Home Then)
barren.linePrev: All the bellies and the bones and the bile?
barren.line: Girl: No, I lingered here with the blankets barren
barren.lineNext: And my own belly big with child
stanza: Girl: No, I lingered here with the blankets barren
And my own belly big with child

barren.linePrev: Or be like the rose that you hold in your hand (Lover, be good to me)
barren.line: That will grow bold in a barren and desolate land
barren.lineNext: Oh, lover, be good to me
stanza: Ah, be love in its disrepute (Lover, be good to me)
That scorches the hillside and salts every root (Lover, be good to me)
And watches the slowin’ and starvin' of troops
And, lover, be good to me (Lover, be good to me)
Be there and just as you stand (Lover, be good to me)
Or be like the rose that you hold in your hand (Lover, be good to me)
That will grow bold in a barren and desolate land
Oh, lover, be good to me

sharon.line: I went to Staten Island, Sharon
stanza: I went to Staten Island, Sharon
To buy myself a mandolin
And I saw the long white dress of love
On a storefront mannequin
Big boat chuggin' back with a belly full of cars
All for something lacy
Some girl's going to see that dress
And crave that day like crazy

sharon.line: When we were kids in Maidstone, Sharon
sharon.lineNext: I went to every wedding in that little town
stanza: When we were kids in Maidstone, Sharon
I went to every wedding in that little town
To see the tears and the kisses
And the pretty lady in the white-lace wedding gown
And walking home on the railroad tracks
Or swinging on the playground swing
Love stimulated my illusions
More than anything

partner.line: And walking home on the railroad tracks

sharon.line: And we sang "Sweet Rose of Sharon, Abide With Me"
sharon.lineNext: Until I ride "The Gospel Ship to Heaven's Jubilee"
stanza: And we sang "Sweet Rose of Sharon, Abide With Me"
Until I ride "The Gospel Ship to Heaven's Jubilee"
And "In That Great Triumphant Morning" my soul will be free
And "My Burdens Will Be Lifted" when my Saviour's face I see

sharon.linePrev: And eighteen bucks went up in smoke
stanza: Sharon, I left my man
At a North Dakota junction
And I came out to The Big Apple here
To face the dream's malfunction
Love's a repetitious danger
You'd think I'd be accustomed to
Well, I do accept the changes
At least better than I used to do

sharon.lineNext: And a family and a farm
stanza: Sharon, you've got a husband
And a family and a farm
I've got the apple of temptation
And a diamond snake around my arm
But you still have your music
And I've still got my eyes on the land and the sky
You sing for your friends and your family
I'll walk green pastures by and by
